commit.message:
BUG: cluster.hierarchy.fcluster: reject t < 1 for maxclust criteria (#26100)

cluster_maxclust_monocrit ends with MC[upper_idx], where MC has n-1 entries and
upper_idx starts at n-1. upper_idx only moves down when some threshold gives
nc <= max_nc, and testing i = n-2 always puts the whole tree in one cluster, so
that test only fails when max_nc < 1. in that one case upper_idx is never lowered
and MC[n-1] is read one past the end of the array.

the file is compiled with boundscheck=False, so nothing catches it and the cutoff
is whatever happens to sit in that memory. with t=0 on six points the result is
six singleton clusters, and feeding a longer MC with a known value in slot n-1
changes the answer, which is what showed where it was reading from.

no t can produce fewer than one cluster, so the input is rejected instead. this
removes the only path that reaches the read. t >= 1 is unchanged, and distance
and inconsistent still take t=0.

commit.message:
TST: linalg: fix Pyodide hang and crash in wrapper GC tests (#26267)

* TST: linalg: skip `test_wrapper_module_collected` on WASM

Loading a second copy of the `_fblas`/`_flapack` extension module
intermittently hangs the Pyodide job until the CI timeout cancels it.

* TST: linalg: use `gc.get_referents` in `test_wrapper_traverses_its_type`

`gc.get_referrers` calls tp_traverse on every tracked object, and on
Pyodide an unrelated extension type trips a fatal 'null function or
function signature mismatch'. `gc.get_referents(func)` only calls the
wrapper's own traverse, which is what the test is about.

* TST:linalg.blas:Modify test_wrapper_traverses_its_type

Update test to check for referents of the function type.

* TST: linalg: skip self-referential recursion test on WASM

`test_self_referential_sequence_raises_recursion_error` overflows the
Pyodide stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) before the
interpreter's recursion limit raises RecursionError, which is a fatal
error that takes down the whole pytest-split group.

---------

MAINT: use OpenBLAS `0.3.34.237.0`

* As discussed in gh-26098, it would be helpful for the SciPy `1.18.2`
release to use the latest OpenBLAS available from `scipy-openblas..`
because it helped the user/situation described in that ticket.

* I believe we no longer bump OpenBLAS using the method used in gh-25669,
because we now have fancy dependency groups and lock/syncing to the
release repo where wheels are built. See
https://github.com/scipy/scipy-release/pull/39, although frankly
some of that is a bit over my head. But, I think for us mortals
this basically means that `pyproject.toml` settings are derived
from the main repo and used in the release repo wheel builds.

* I did also change the matching `pixi` manifest OpenBLAS
pins and ran `pixi lock` locally using version `0.81.0`. The
output of that command only reported OpenBLAS-related changes
and the `pixi.lock` diff appears to only mutate `scipy-openblas..`
things.

commit.message:
BUG: signal.sepfir2d: reject filters too long for the input axis (#26001)

`_fir_mirror_symmetric` reflects an out-of-range index only once, so it
needs at least 2*(len(filt)//2) samples along the axis it filters. On a
shorter axis it read past both ends of the input, and once len(filt)//2
exceeded the axis length it also wrote outside the output; the values
returned were whatever the adjacent heap happened to hold. Validate both
axes in FIRsepsym2d instead of relying on the caller (gh-24681).

The bound is exact rather than the len(filt) <= n that the removed TODO
suggested: len(filt) == n + 1 stays in bounds and agrees with a
mirror-symmetric reference convolution, so it remains accepted.

Also removes the ASAN suppression and the two xfail markers that hid
this, and pins the expected dtype in test_sepfir2d_strided_3, which the
xfail had been masking as well.

BUG: sparse: fix broadcast-assigning a lower-dim sparse array into higher-dim COO (#25989)

* BUG: sparse: fix broadcast-assigning a lower-dim sparse array into higher-dim COO

`coo_array.__setitem__` broadcasts a sparse right-hand side to the target
region via `_get_sparse_data_and_coords`. When the RHS has fewer dimensions
than the target (leading axes need prepending, `len_diff > 0`), two bugs on
that code path made it always raise:

- `np.zeroslike` is a typo for `np.zeros_like`, raising AttributeError.
- After that, `x_coords` was rebuilt as a `tuple`, but the broadcasting loop
  below item-assigns `x_coords[i] = ...`, which raises TypeError on a tuple.

Both are fixed so sparse-RHS broadcast assignment with prepended axes works,
matching NumPy broadcasting semantics. Adds a regression test.

Fixes gh-25965.

* DEV: add check_nondefault_device linter for array-API device propagation

Add an AST-based linter that flags internal array-creation calls
(`xp.zeros`, `xp.full`, `xp.arange`, `xp.asarray(<literal>)`,
`xp.fft.r?fftfreq`, ...) that omit an explicit `device=`. Such calls place
the result on the backend's default device, which raises a device-mismatch
error when the array is later combined with an input on a non-default device
(see gh-22680).

The checker is wired into `spin lint` (and hence `pixi run lint`), with a
standalone `pixi run check-nondefault-device` task for targeted runs. A
`# skip device check` pragma allows genuine standalone-scratch arrays. Unit
tests cover the flagging rule, exemptions, and pragma handling.

Thread a `device` argument through `_elementwise_iterative_method._loop` so
the bookkeeping/result arrays (`active`, status, counters) are created on the
same device as the input; callers pass `device=xp_device(...)`. Also drop the
now-unnecessary `xp.asarray(_EINPROGRESS)` scalar wrapper.

In `_array_api._asarray`, mark the throwaway `xp.asarray(3)` used only to
obtain a coerced namespace with `# skip device check`.
